environment.description: Same Go binary deployed inside a Podman container on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (myapp_webhook_t). The policy module (compiled via checkmodule/semodule_package) defines the process domain myapp_webhook_t with the following constraints: (1) allow myapp_webhook_t myapp_secret_t:file { read open getattr }; — the secret file is labeled myapp_secret_t and readable. (2) The container runs with --security-opt label=type:myapp_webhook_t. (3) A companion network namespace policy (via systemd-networkd) applies a tc-netem qdisc on the container's veth interface adding uniform random delay of 0-5ms to all egress packets (tc qdisc add dev veth_myapp root netem delay 2.5ms 2.5ms distribution normal). (4) Additionally, the host runs a BPF-based scheduling noise injector (sched_ext class) that introduces 0-3ms random preemption delays to any process in the myapp_webhook_t SELinux context. The combination of network jitter injection and CPU scheduling noise makes timing measurements statistically indistinguishable across correct vs incorrect signature bytes, requiring >10^6 samples per byte position to achieve significance — effectively blocking the timing side-channel within any practical attack window.

config.network_jitter: tc qdisc netem on container veth: delay 2.5ms 2.5ms distribution normal
config.cpu_noise: sched_ext BPF program injecting 0-3ms random preemption for myapp_webhook_t processes
config.combined_noise_floor: ~5.5ms uniform random noise vs ~0.5ns timing signal per byte
